source_text:
Ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἐργάτης μετὰ παρρησίας λαμβάνει τὸν ἄρτον τοῦ ἔργου αὐτοῦ, ὁ νωθρὸς καὶ παρειμένος οὐκ ἀντοφθαλμεῖ τῷ ἐργοπαρέκτῃ αὐτοῦ,
δέον οὖν ἐστὶν προθύμους ἡμᾶς εἶναι εἰς ἀγαθοποιΐαν: ἐξ αὐτοῦ γάρ ἐστιν τὰ πάντα.
προλέγει γὰρ ἡμῖν: Ἰδοὺ ὁ κύριος, καὶ ὁ μισθὸς αὐτοῦ πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ, ἀποδοῦναι ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ.
προτρέπεται οὖν ἡμᾶς πιστεύοντας ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας ἐπ’ αὐτῷ, μὴ ἀργοὺς μηδὲ παρειμένους εἶναι ἐπὶ πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθόν.
τὸ καύχημα ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ παρρησία ἔστω ἐν αὐτῷ: ὑποτασσώμεθα τῷ θελήματι αὐτοῦ: κατανοήσωμεν τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ, πῶς τῷ θελήματι αὐτοῦ λειτουργοῦσιν παρεστῶτες.
λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή: Μύριαι μυριάδες παρειστήκεισαν αὐτῷ, καὶ χίλιαι χιλιάδες ἐλειτούργουν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐκέκραγον, Ἅγιος, ἅγιος, ἅγιος κύριος σαβαώθ, πλήρης πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ.
καὶ ἡμεῖς, οὖν, ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ συναχθέντες τῇ συνειδήσει, ὡς ἐξ ἑνὸς στόματος βοήσωμεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐκτενῶς εἰς τὸ μετόχους ἡμᾶς γενέσθαι τῶν μεγάλων καὶ ἐνδόξων ἐπαγγελιῶν αὐτοῦ.
λέγει γάρ: Ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν, καὶ οὕς οὐκ ἤκουσεν, καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἀνέβη, ὅσα ἡτοίμασεν κύριος τοῖς ὑπομένουσιν αὐτόν.
thought_title: The good worker and the reward for good work
orientation: The author urges the Corinthians to be eager for good work and to submit to the will of God, holding up the angels as the pattern.
pass_a_gloss: The good worker receives with boldness the bread of his work, but the idle and slack man does not look in the face of the giver of his work. Therefore it is necessary for us to be eager for the doing of good, for from him are all things. For he foretells to us, Behold the lord, and his reward is before his face, to pay back to each according to his work. Therefore he calls us forward, as believing from the whole heart upon him, not to be idle nor slack toward every good work. Let our boast and our boldness be in him. Let us be in submission to his will. Let us observe the whole crowd of his angels, how they do ministry to his will standing beside him. For the scripture says, Ten thousand ten thousands stood beside him, and a thousand thousands did ministry to him, and they cried out, Holy, holy, holy lord Sabaoth, all creation is full of his glory. We therefore, having been gathered together upon the same place in harmony with conscience, as from one mouth let us cry out to him earnestly, so that we become sharers of his great and glorious promises. For he says, Eye did not see, and ear did not hear, and upon heart of man it did not go up, how many things the lord prepared for those who wait for him.

choices.why: keeps the noun for good doing plain and avoids polishing into virtue language

choices.english: let us be in submission to his will
choices.why: uses the brief glossary English submission for the verb of submission
rejected: let us subject ourselves to his will

choices.why: uses the brief glossary English ministry and avoids banned service
uses the brief glossary English harmony for concord of the gathered church

pass_b_english: The good worker receives the bread his work has earned with confidence. The lazy and slack worker cannot face the one who gives him work. So we must be eager for the doing of good, for all things come from him.

For he tells us beforehand, "See the Lord, and his reward is before him, to repay each one according to his work" (Isaiah 40:10). So he urges us, since we believe in him with our whole heart, not to grow idle or slack in any good work.

Let our boast and our confidence be in him. Let us be in submission to his will. Let us consider the whole host of his angels, how they stand beside him and do ministry to his will. For Scripture says, "Ten thousand times ten thousand stood beside him, and a thousand thousands did ministry to him" (Daniel 7:10), and they cried out, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole creation is full of his glory" (Isaiah 6:3).

So we too should gather together in harmony with one conscience and cry to him earnestly as with one voice, so we may become sharers in his great and glorious promises. For Scripture says, "Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not entered the human heart, what the Lord has prepared for those who wait for him" (1 Corinthians 2:9).

problems.why: The source has a verbless “Behold the Lord,” with no verb of coming.
problems.fix: See, the Lord, and his reward is before his face, to repay each according to his work.
problems.ruling: Source is verbless ‘Ἰδοὺ ὁ κύριος’; ‘comes’ is added. Though LXX Isaiah 40:10 has ‘ἰδοὺ κύριος’ without a verb, the added verb is minor but unsupported.

edits.old: See, the Lord comes, and his reward is before him, to repay each one according to his work
edits.new: See the Lord, and his reward is before him, to repay each one according to his work

fixed: Removed added 'comes': source Ἰδοὺ ὁ κύριος is verbless with no verb of coming.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ἰδοὺ ὁ κύριος, καὶ ὁ μισθὸς αὐτοῦ πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ, ἀποδοῦναι ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: Isaiah 40:10 has reward with him and work before him, not repayment to each according to his work.
last_rejected.fix: "See the Lord, and his reward is before him, to repay each according to his work" (Isaiah 62:11; Revelation 22:12).
last_rejected.ruling: 1 Clement's text itself conflates Isaiah 40:10 with Isa 62:11 and Prov 24:12 ("κατὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ"); attributing to Isaiah is a reasonable source reference, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.source_quote: ὅσα ἡτοίμασεν κύριος τοῖς ὑπομένουσιν αὐτόν
last_rejected.why: 1 Corinthians 2:9 says God prepared this for those who love him, not the Lord for those who wait.
last_rejected.fix: "what the Lord has prepared for those who wait for him" (Isaiah 64:4; cf. 1 Corinthians 2:9).
last_rejected.ruling: 1 Clement 34:8 quotes a free variant ("τοῖς ὑπομένουσιν αὐτόν"), and the English faithfully renders it; the 1 Cor 2:9 citation is the standard parallel.
